Marcus Aurelius on virtue

Marcus Aurelius (121–180) approaches virtue within Stoicism. He urged attention to what lies within one's agency, acceptance of nature's order, and justice toward fellow rational beings. Systematically, the teaching links ethics, self-discipline, cosmopolitanism into a practical and theoretical whole. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets virtue most directly—useful for searches such as “marcus aurelius quotes on virtue.”

How to use this page

Start with the shortest passage, then compare tone across sources. Return to the Marcus Aurelius thinker page for biography and to the virtue theme for other voices on the same question.
